half_alu_fma12.byte4_modifiers.claim: byte+4 is a modifier byte, not part of an opaque residue. Measured at length selector 3: value 0x03/0x07/0x0b/0x0f -> |a|*b + c; 0x13/0x17/0x1b/0x1f -> |a|*b - c (bit 4 negates the third operand); bit 7 additionally RELEASES (zeroes) the byte+5 source lane; the 0x20..0x3f family produces a coherent but unmodelled result.
half_alu_fma12.byte4_modifiers.evidence: EXP-0203 raw/g17p_run31..32 byte+4 sweeps, plus the offline re-derivation from EXP-0180's committed raw in analysis/fit_model_offline.py.
half_alu_fma12.byte4_modifiers.status: PARTIAL -- reported as a liveness+partial-semantic map, not as a complete modifier decode.

half_alu_fma12.ext.claim: `ext` is not one 64-bit field. Proposed split, with what each part was MEASURED to do at (opsel 6, length selector 3): bits 32..33 = LENGTH SELECTOR (already known); bits 34..39 = arithmetic/modifier bits, live at bits 3,4,5,6,7 with bit 2 showing no effect on any of the three arms; **bits 40..47 = `srcC`, the third fp16 source half-register descriptor** h = (reg<<1)|is_high with bit 7 a DON'T-CARE; bits 48..55 (byte+6) live at bits 2..7 depending on carrier; bits 56..63 (byte+7) live at bit 4; bits 64..71 (byte+8) and 72..79 (byte+9) live at bit 1 only; bits 80..87 (byte+10) live at bit 0; bits 88..95 (byte+11) showed a single payload on all three arms.
half_alu_fma12.ext.evidence: EXP-0203 analysis/ext_bytes.json: 2048 values x 3 arms x 2 runs; byte+5 has 256/256 hardware identity preserved AND 256/256 full-vector oracle match on every arm; bit-7 don't-care 128/128.
half_alu_fma12.ext.inertness_caveat: NOTHING here is declared inert. byte+10 is the demonstration: a single payload over all 256 values on carrier A, and TWO payloads on carriers B and C in the same runs. Per FIELD-SWEEP-PROTOCOL section 9 and RE_EXPERIMENT_PROCESS_CORRECTIONS.md section 7 an inert claim needs a positive control in the dimension the bit would control and three structurally different carrier classes; byte+11's correct status is `inert in this exact tested envelope (opsel 6, length selector 3, three compute carriers, 16-GPR readback); global role unknown`.

half_pack.byte0.claim: db.json pins ALL EIGHT bits of byte0 in `match` (0x18), so every db-expressible encoding writes r1. byte0's HIGH nibble is the destination GPR and its LOW nibble (8) is the family tag -- the same defect class as DEF-0180-1 one family over.
half_pack.byte0.evidence: EXP-0203: the instruction had to be built byte by byte to express any other destination. Arms HP_C/HP_D run the same instruction at destination nibble 7 (`78 0d 18 11`) and the host oracle matches 256/256 there as well, so the nibble is a real destination selector and not a fixed opcode bit.
half_pack.byte0.status: REPORTED, not applied -- db.json is the orchestrator's file.

half_pack.length_gate.claim: Independent HARDWARE confirmation of DEF-0154-1. `isadb.instr_length` accepts byte0 == 0x18 as a 4-byte `half_pack` only when byte+1 == 0x05, so our own tokenizer returned `<unknown>` for the anchor `18 0d 18 11` and disagreed with itself on 11 of the 256 byte+1 values -- while the HARDWARE consumed exactly four bytes for ALL 256 (all four 2-byte length markers survived in every case, every arm, every run). The byte+1 gate is not a length condition.
half_pack.length_gate.evidence: EXP-0203 raw/g17p_run31..32: hw_markers == 4 on 256/256 values x 4 arms x 2 runs; `tok_instr` recorded alongside and NEVER gated on.

half_pack.source_release.claim: At byte+2 = 0x18 the instruction ZEROES both named source half-lanes (opflags 3 source release). WHICH lane is zeroed follows the descriptor's value, so this is part of the field's semantics, not a constant side effect.
half_pack.source_release.evidence: EXP-0203 pilot01: every release-free candidate model scored 2/80; with the release the arithmetic member scores 80/80. Confirmed on 2048 gated field cases.

half_pack.write_target.claim: `half_pack` writes the destination's HIGH 16 bits and PRESERVES its LOW 16 bits. Its byte0-low-nibble-0 sibling writes the LOW half. The db semantics string calls this a 'pack'; what was measured is a per-lane fp16 ALU op on the HIGH lane, which is what makes a `half2` operation take one instruction per lane.
half_pack.write_target.evidence: EXP-0203 raw/g17p_run31..32, 4 arms x 512 field cases, full-post-state oracle match 100%.

harness.anchor_loss.claim: SELF-REPORTED HARNESS DEFECT. `harness/run.py::classify` returns `ok` when the arm's anchor observation is None, so a LOST anchor silently becomes a pass for every case in that arm. It happened once: in g17p_run32 arm F12_EXT_C's anchor dispatch was an `...InnocentVictim` (a sibling context's GPU error/recovery), so 2048 of that run's outcome labels defaulted to `ok`.
harness.anchor_loss.fix: classify() should return `invalid_run` when the anchor is missing. Recorded rather than patched mid-experiment: the raw is append-only and the runs are already gated.
harness.anchor_loss.impact: NONE on any verdict. The promotion gate does not read `outcome` for movement -- it compares observed post-state digests against run1's (clean) anchor, and the oracle is computed per case from that case's own pre-dump. Cross-run agreement over the affected arm is 2047/2048.

axes.compiler_recipe_basis: The instruction is built byte by byte from documented rules -- necessarily, because db.json pins byte0 and an assembler cannot express any other destination. DONOR REGIONS DECLARED: bytes +6..+11 keep the values our OWN `k_hfma_abs` compiled to, and byte+2's opsel 6 is the compiler-observed hfma selector. Not `canonical-recipe-proven`: those six tail bytes were not generated from rules.
axes.encoding_geometry_basis: Gate A ledger on 64 of 64 dispatched cases in both runs: requested bytes == actual bytes read back from the dispatched artifact, and the value decoded from those ACTUAL bytes equals the requested value in 64/64. 16 distinct requested values -> 16 distinct actual encodings per arm, differing ONLY inside bits 4..7. Framing invariant: all four 2-byte length markers survived on 16/16 values in every arm and every run.
axes.liveness_basis: 10 of 11 decidable values per arm move the observable against the arm's single anchor observation (the 11th IS the anchor value). Detection-power control `__ctl_live_srcA`: 8/8 oracle matches with 8 distinct payloads in every arm and both runs.
axes.reproducibility_basis: Two carriers (different Metal buffer signatures) x two disjoint register/readback plans x two seed sets x two run orders (forward g17p_run31, reverse g17p_run32); 0 cross-run disagreements; immutable raw; hashed authored sources; repeatable analysis scripts.
axes.semantics_basis: An independent host predictor, fitted offline on EXP-0180's committed raw BEFORE this experiment's contract was frozen, predicts the COMPLETE 16-word post-state from each case's own pre-dump. It matched 11/11 decidable values per arm in BOTH runs (44/44 arm-values), and 8 competing frozen models were rejected. Four adversarial cases per arm (null block, opsel change, destination override) all produced the required NON-match.

half_alu_fma12.dst.label: hardware-run
half_alu_fma12.dst.note:
**THE 12-BYTE FORM'S DESTINATION NIBBLE HAD NEVER BEEN SWEPT.** validation.json's previous note (EXP-0196) reported '768 records over 256 distinct values' for this row; those records carry fstart 8 / fwidth 8 -- byte+1 -- and are the field EXP-0183 RENAMED to `srcA`. A 4-bit field cannot have 256 distinct values; that is the tell. EXP-0180's only bits-4..7 arm is `DSTNIB` (32 records) and it runs on `half_alu_ext8`, the EIGHT-byte form. EXP-0196's other two findings were right and are what this experiment fixed: no host oracle existed anywhere in those records, and the read-back was not isolated.
SEMANTICS (host-oracle verified, every decidable value, both gated runs, four arms): the nibble selects GPR n; the fp16 result lands in r[n]'s LOW 16 bits with r[n]'s HIGH 16 bits PRESERVED; no other architectural register changes. Model r[n].lo = fp16_rn(|h(byte+1)| * h(byte+3) - h(byte+5)) at byte+2 = 0x06, byte+4 = 0x13, where h(d) -> (GPR (d & 0x7F) >> 1, half d & 1).
COVERAGE, exact: 16 of 16 values dispatched in each of 4 arms = 64 dispatches per run; 11 decidable per arm; 5 per arm are overwritten AFTER the block by that arm's own infrastructure (the dump index register and the four length markers) and are recorded `carrier_undecidable`, never `inert`. The two readback plans are complementary, so all 16 values are decidable in at least one arm and 6 in both.
ROUNDING: the fused (single-rounding) FMA model and the two-rounding model give different predictions in 8 of 4244 fma12 cases; the FUSED model matched in 8 of 8 and the two-rounding model in 0 of 8. No case in this carrier produced a subnormal or overflowing prediction, so flush-to-zero and overflow behaviour are UNTESTED here.
half_alu_fma12.dst.range: 16 of 16 encodable values decidable in >=1 arm over 4 arms; 64 dispatched, 64 distinct encodings

axes.encoding_geometry_basis: Gate A ledger on 2048 of 2048 dispatched cases per arm x 3 arms x 2 runs, 2048 distinct actual encodings. Framing is NOT invariant here and that is the point: byte+4's low two bits are the length selector, so 128 of its 256 values change the consumed length (measured by the marker chain) and are excluded from every semantic claim.
axes.liveness_basis: byte+5 gives 29 distinct payloads over 256 values on all three arms. byte+4/+6/+7 give 5..11. byte+8/+9/+10 give 2. byte+11 gives 1 on all three arms and is NOT declared inert. byte+10 is the cautionary case: 1 payload on carrier A, 2 on carriers B and C in the same runs.
axes.reproducibility_basis: Three arms, two run orders, 1 cross-run disagreement in 5760 covered arm-values; one isolated GPU-hang fault at byte+7 = 0xEE on arm F12_EXT_C in run31 only, and one InnocentVictim that cost arm F12_EXT_C its anchor observation in run32 (see RESULTS.md -> Contamination).
axes.semantics_basis: bits 40..47 (byte+5) are SEMANTICALLY MAPPED: 256/256 full-post-state oracle match on three arms in both runs, with bit 7 a measured don't-care (128/128 value pairs identical). The rest of `ext` is a liveness map with per-bit resolution, not a semantic map.

half_pack.dstlo.label: hardware-run
half_pack.dstlo.note:
**MISNAMED IN db.json: this is a SOURCE half-register descriptor, not a destination.** `half_pack` (byte0 = 0x18) is the high-lane sibling of the byte0-low-nibble-0 half-ALU family and shares its operand shape; byte+1 is a source descriptor h = (reg<<1)|is_high with **bit 7 a measured don't-care**. Model, 256/256 in both gated runs on four arms: r[byte0>>4].hi = fp16_rn(h(byte+1) + h(byte+3)), the destination's LOW half preserved, and **both named source half-lanes zeroed** (the byte+2 = 0x18 opflags-3 source release).
DETECTION POWER: 256 values give 29 distinct payloads per arm. That is the PREDICTED number, not a weakness: 16 GPRs x 2 halves are reachable, bit 7 is ignored, and every descriptor naming an unseeded GPR reads 0. The oracle predicts WHICH of the 29 each value produces and was right on all 256.
OPERAND ORDER IS NOT ESTABLISHED: the measured operation is commutative, so this sweep cannot separate byte+1 from byte+3 by role. The proposed name follows the family's positional convention, not an observation.
half_pack.dstlo.range: 256 of 256 encodable values decidable in >=1 arm over 4 arms; 1024 dispatched, 1024 distinct encodings
